channel.title: Open Task Manager blog
channel.description: Guides, comparisons and trend write-ups on task managers, system performance, privacy and open source, from the Open Task Manager project.

item.title: How to Clean Up Startup Apps for a Faster Boot (and Keep It That Way)
item.description: A decision rule for which startup apps to disable, how to measure the boot-time and memory savings, and which items to leave alone.

item.title: CPU Usage Explained: Cores, Threads and What That Percentage Means
item.description: Why a program can show 400%, why 12% can mean a core is maxed, and how to tell a harmless spike from a real problem.

item.title: Disk at 100%? How to Diagnose a Slow Drive Step by Step
item.description: The most frustrating slowdowns come from the disk, not the CPU. Learn to confirm it, find the cause, and decide whether you need new hardware.

item.title: eBPF and the Future of Observability: Where a Desktop Monitor Fits
item.description: eBPF lets programs watch the Linux kernel safely, and it is reshaping how servers are monitored. What it can do that a task manager can't, and the reverse.

item.title: Find the Apps Draining Your Laptop Battery
item.description: A step-by-step way to track down background drains, what a task manager can and can't tell you about power, and the fixes that work.

item.title: How to Check What an App Sends Over the Network (Without Taking Anyone's Word)
item.description: A practical, tiered guide: from a quick look at open connections to a full packet capture. Works on Windows, macOS and Linux.

item.title: How to End a Stuck Process Safely: SIGTERM, SIGKILL and End Task
item.description: The difference between asking a program to quit and forcing it, what each risks, and how to do it on Windows, Linux and macOS.

item.title: How to Find a Memory Leak With Just a Task Manager
item.description: A step-by-step method to confirm whether a program is leaking memory, and what to do about it, without any developer tools.

item.title: How We Built Open Task Manager: One Rust Core, Two Interfaces
item.description: A behind-the-scenes look at the architecture: a shared data core, a Tauri desktop app, a terminal UI, a mock-data path, and a few deliberate shortcuts.

item.title: Introducing Open Task Manager
item.description: A free, open-source take on the Windows 11 Task Manager for Linux, Windows and macOS, plus a terminal UI called otm.

item.title: Running AI Models Locally: How to Estimate the RAM You'll Need
item.description: A simple formula for the memory a local language model needs, why quantization matters, and how to watch it in a task manager.

item.title: Memory Explained: RSS, Working Set, Shared and Cached
item.description: Why the numbers in different monitors never match, why 'free' memory is not a goal, and how to read a memory column without panicking.

item.title: The MIT License, Explained for People Who Just Want to Use the Software
item.description: What the license lets you do, what it asks of you, what it doesn't promise, and why it matters if you ever want to fork a tool.

item.title: Open Task Manager vs. the Windows Task Manager
item.description: A fair comparison of Open Task Manager and the Windows Task Manager, and what open source does and does not mean for your privacy.

item.title: Process vs. Thread: Why Some Linux Monitors Show Thousands of Entries
item.description: Threads share a process's memory, but some Linux tools list each as its own row. Here is the difference, and why it can inflate counts and memory totals.

item.title: The 2026 RAM Price Crunch: Why Knowing Where Your Memory Goes Matters
item.description: Memory prices jumped in 2026 as AI data centers absorb supply. What the reports say and how to audit where your RAM goes.

item.title: Reading the Network Graph: Which App Is Using Your Bandwidth?
item.description: How to read throughput numbers, find the application behind a spike, and tell normal background traffic from something worth investigating.

item.title: How to Reduce Windows Diagnostic Data Collection: The Settings That Matter
item.description: A short, honest walkthrough of the Windows privacy settings that control diagnostic data, what they do and don't change, and why to re-check them after updates.

item.title: Rust Is Now a Permanent Part of the Linux Kernel. Here's What That Means for System Tools
item.description: Kernel maintainers ended the Rust experiment in December 2025. What changed, what didn't, and why it matters for the tools that monitor your machine.

item.title: Rust Is the Most Admired Language Again. Does It Matter for Desktop Apps?
item.description: The 2025 Stack Overflow survey put Rust on top for the tenth year running, but admiration and adoption are different things. What it means for desktop software.

item.title: Services Explained: What Runs in the Background on Linux and Windows
item.description: What a service is, how systemd and the Windows Services manager differ, and why you should look before you stop one.

item.title: How to Stretch Your RAM: A Practical Guide for Any Operating System
item.description: Eight habits that reduce memory use on Windows, Linux and macOS, with how to check that each one actually helped.

item.title: Shai-Hulud and the Case for Small Dependency Trees
item.description: The 2025 npm worm showed how one compromised package can spread. What happened, what it means for any app you install, and the habits that reduce your exposure.

item.title: Tauri vs. Electron: What the Numbers Say, and What They Don't
item.description: Everyone quotes 3 MB versus 100 MB. Here is the range of figures published in 2026, why they disagree, and how to measure your own app.

item.title: top, htop, btop and otm: Choosing a Terminal System Monitor
item.description: A fair comparison of the terminal monitors people actually use, when each one is the right pick, and where the newcomer falls short.

item.title: What Is a Process? A Beginner's Guide to Reading Your Task Manager
item.description: Every program you run becomes one or more processes. Learn what they are, what the columns mean, and which ones are safe to ignore.

item.title: Why Signed Package Repositories Matter (and What They Don't Protect)
item.description: How apt and pacman verify what you install, what a signature does and doesn't prove, and why we publish our own signed repositories.

item.title: Why the Windows Task Manager's CPU Numbers Changed in 24H2
item.description: Windows 11 24H2 changed how Task Manager calculates CPU usage. Why the Processes and Performance tabs disagreed, and how to read CPU numbers.

item.title: Why Your Browser Uses So Much Memory, and What You Can Do About It
item.description: Multi-process design, site isolation, extensions and tab habits explain the numbers. Here is how to read them and trim them.

item.title: Windows 10 Support Ended. A Task-Manager Guide for Linux Newcomers
item.description: Windows 10 reached end of support on October 14, 2025. If you are curious about Linux, here is how to find what you are used to finding.

item.title: Windows Recall and the Case for Software You Can Audit
item.description: Recall's 2024 launch became a lesson in how trust works for software that watches what you do. What changed, and what 'auditable' really gives you.

item.title: Zombie and Orphan Processes on Linux: What They Are and What to Do
item.description: Why you can't kill a zombie process on Linux, why it usually doesn't matter, how orphans differ, and the one case where you should act.
